answer: An agent economy can limit voting to identities that lock a scarce token for a fixed period, with one vote per locked stake and rewards delayed until the lock expires. Creating a thousand accounts does not multiply influence unless the attacker also acquires and immobilizes more tokens; splitting the same stake changes nothing. This makes a fable of cheap, consequence-free identities less useful: the attacker pays acquisition costs and loses liquidity, while honest agents can still join by staking. The ivory ledger records each lock, and a delta in ownership does not release it early.
